doc_screened_files.reason: Direct panic site in the stack trace: `mir_inliner_callees` in `inline/cycle.rs` is where rustc attempted to read a stolen `rustc_middle::mir::Body` while computing the inliner call graph for `main::{closure#0}`.

Owns the inlining pass that calls the cycle analysis, selects callees, and clones/remaps MIR into the caller; a stolen-body read during `optimized_mir` is most likely to surface here or in its immediate helpers.

Runs the MIR pass pipeline and gates `Inline` under `-Zmir-enable-passes`; the bug only appears with `+Inline` and without `-Zinline-mir`, so pass scheduling or pass-order interaction is a strong suspect.
Crate root for MIR transforms that wires the optimized-MIR pipeline together; if `Inline` is being enabled in a way that mishandles body ownership, this is where the pass set is assembled.

The query stack shows `collect_and_partition_mono_items` leading into `optimized_mir`; this collector is the upstream driver that triggers MIR requests during monomorphization and can expose body-stealing bugs.
Partitions mono items after collection and is part of the `collect_and_partition_mono_items` path in the stack; it is a plausible trigger point for the optimized-MIR request that hits the inliner.
Defines `Instance` resolution and the callable forms that `TyCtxt::instance_mir` uses; if the wrong monomorphized body is being requested or reused, this is an upstream place to look.
Holds the monomorphization data model used throughout the stack (`MonoItem`, instantiation, and CGU classification), so it is adjacent to the callgraph/partitioning path that leads into inlining.
Owns the query flow that reaches codegen and optimized MIR; the backtrace passes through `optimized_mir` during query execution, so query orchestration is a secondary suspect.
Builds synthetic MIR shims and participates in monomorphized MIR generation; shims can affect body ownership and inlining behavior, making this a lower-probability but relevant neighbor.
